author: raymond91125
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Scope revised 2026-09-08.** `GO:0043041` is on the obsoletion list alongside `GO:0043042` — reasoning and retraction: [go-ontology#30872](https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/issues/30872#issuecomment-5544118855). The migration table below was also corrected after reading the three papers in **full text** rather than abstracts; all three annotations move, and EntF's moves with a **different reference**. Earlier versions of this ticket said otherwise.

[Written by Claude]

## What is changing

Both terms are being obsoleted as MF-in-BP. They are 1:1 with the *same* single molecular function — adenylation plus thioesterification onto a carrier protein, one catalysed reaction — and that MF is being added as `GO:7770118 amino acid--[peptidyl-carrier protein] ligase activity` in [go-ontology#32568](https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/pull/32568).

| Term | Action |
|---|---|
| `GO:0043041` amino acid activation for nonribosomal peptide biosynthetic process | obsolete |
| `GO:0043042` amino acid adenylylation by nonribosomal peptide synthase | obsolete |

`consider: GO:7770118` on both. **No `replaced_by`** — that would be BP→MF, and `GO:0019184` is not a valid target either, since `GO:0043041` is `part_of` it rather than `is_a`.

## Annotations to review

268 annotations across the two terms, of which **3 are experimental**. Those 3 are the review scope here; the remainder are IBA, ISS and IEA from the standard pipelines and are handled by the normal obsoletion process, not by this ticket.

| Group | Gene | Current | Recommended |
|---|---|---|---|
| EcoCyc (@amandamackie) | EntF | `GO:0043041` IDA PMID:1826089 | drop it; add `GO:7770118` IDA **PMID:9485415** (different reference — see below); retire `GO:0016779` |
| FlyBase (@hattrill) | ebony | `GO:0043042` IDA PMID:12900414 | `GO:7770118` IDA PMID:12900414 |
| MGI (@LiNiMGI) | Aasdh | `GO:0043041` IDA PMID:24467666 | `GO:7770118` IDA PMID:24467666 |

`GO:7770118` requires **both** halves of the reaction — ATP-dependent activation of the amino acid *and* its transfer as a thioester onto the phosphopantetheine group. Each paper was checked against that.

### EntF — reference swap needed

The 1991 abstract says it *"confirmed the expected activities of EntF"*, but the Results do not support the loading step:

> *"...verified that it does indeed **activate L-serine** at least transiently via an L-seryl-AMP intermediate as indicated by the L-serine-dependent ATP-[32P]PPi exchange... **However, we were unable to detect measurable loading of the partially purified wild-type enzyme with [14C]serine.**"* (PMID:1826089)

The authors are explicit that the carrier step was unproven at the time — *"in none of the multienzyme complexes noted has it actually been proven that the phosphopantetheine thiolate is the enzyme thiol to which the activated amino acid is transferred"* — and they could not localise the cofactor (*"two serine residues are potential sites for its attachment"*).

So PMID:1826089 supports adenylation only, which is what `GO:0043041` said and no more. It cannot carry to `GO:7770118`.

**PMID:9485415** (Gehring, Mori & Walsh 1998, the reconstitution paper) does:

> *"the mutant holo-EntF **retained the ability to adenylate serine and to autoacylate itself by thioester formation between serine and its attached phosphopantetheine cofactor**."*

EntF already carries `GO:0016779 nucleotidyltransferase activity` IDA from that same reference — a vague grandparent term standing in for this reaction. `GO:7770118` replaces it properly, so this is worth doing on its own merits.

Note `group-contacts.csv` flags EcoCyc as not receiving automatic replacement of obsolete terms, so the drop may need doing by hand.

### ebony — straight move

The Ser611Ala mutant (the phosphopantetheine attachment serine) separates the two activities cleanly: adenylation *"indistinguishable from wild type"*, thioester loading down 98%, and all five products absent by mass spectrometry. The paper's conclusion:

> *"Ebony selects specifically the amino acid β-alanine, activates it as aminoacyladenylate, and binds it as thioester of the 4′-phosphopantetheinyl group linked to Ser611."* (PMID:12900414)

`GO:0003833 beta-alanyl amine synthase activity` **stays** — the same mutant shows these are separable activities, not duplicates. `GO:0003833` is the overall conjugation reaction; `GO:7770118` is the loading half that survives loss of product formation.

### Aasdh — straight move

The S591A phosphopantetheine-site mutant gives the same control:

> *"no incorporation was detected with the S591A-ACSF4-U26 mutant, indicating the requirement for the phosphopantetheine group, which presumably serves as the acceptor"*; *"incorporation of [3H]β-alanine was totally dependent on the presence of a nucleotide triphosphate"* (PMID:24467666)

Purified protein, KM values determined, mechanism stated as *"formation of an aminoacyl adenylate followed by transfer of the acyl group to form a (thio)ester."*

Aasdh has no other informative annotation — MF is `molecular_function` ND — so this is the one case where the obsoletion would otherwise lose information outright.

## Why the NRP scoping went

Both the ebony and Aasdh papers describe a **single** activation module, not a multimodular NRPS, and neither protein makes a nonribosomal peptide. The ebony authors note that genuine nonribosomal dipeptide synthesis *"would require two amino acid activation modules in addition to a functional domain for condensation... as well as a thioesterase activity for peptide release,"* and that evidence for this in higher eukaryotes *"is still lacking."* Aasdh's proposed role is an unidentified post-translational or post-transcriptional modification.

`GO:7770118` is deliberately not NRP-scoped (the `part_of GO:0019184` axiom was dropped during review of #32568), which is what allows all three annotations to land on it.

## On ebony's products

@rozaru — thank you for the correction on ebony. For the record, the full text reports **five** mass-spectrometry-confirmed products, not two: β-alanyl-histamine, β-alanyl-dopamine, β-alanyl-tyramine, β-alanyl-octopamine and β-alanyl-serotonin. Dopamine gave *"~94% reduction... almost complete conversion into product."* None of this affects the migration above, but it is direct IDA evidence for NBAD synthesis by ebony.

Your suggestion to reparent `GO:0120576` under `GO:0019184` is worth a separate ticket rather than settling inside an obsoletion. I would push back — `GO:0019184` requires peptide bond formation and sits under `GO:0043043 peptide biosynthetic process`, and the ebony authors' own reasoning above distinguishes these conjugates from peptides. Separately, **ebony is not currently annotated to `GO:0120576` at all**, which looks like a gap regardless.

## Sequence

1. [go-ontology#32568](https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/pull/32568) merges — `GO:7770118`
2. The three migrations above
3. Obsoletion notice to go-announcements
4. Obsoletion PR for both terms

Steps 3 and 4 wait on 1–2.

author: raymond91125
body:
> [!NOTE]
> **Retracted — see the revised issue description above.** `GO:0043041` is *not* being kept; it is obsoleted alongside `GO:0043042`. Reasoning: [go-ontology#30872](https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/issues/30872#issuecomment-5544118855). The scoping question below no longer applies.

[Written by Claude]

Scope change — please read before reviewing. **`GO:0043041` is no longer proposed for obsoletion.** Only `GO:0043042` is.

The reasoning is on geneontology/go-ontology#30872 ([comment](https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/issues/30872#issuecomment-5534068928)). In short: loading an amino acid onto a carrier protein involves two molecular functions, not one — the ligase (`GO:7770118`) and the carrier (`GO:0140414`) — and in type II systems those are two separate gene products. That makes `GO:0043041` a legitimate multi-MF biological process rather than a molecular function wearing a BP label. `GO:0043042` names the reaction alone and is still 1:1 with the new MF.

## What this means for each of you

| Group | Gene | Term | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| @amandamackie (EcoCyc) | EntF | `GO:0043041` | **no action needed** — term is being kept |
| @LiNiMGI (MGI) | Aasdh | `GO:0043041` | term kept, but see below |
| @hattrill (FlyBase) | ebony | `GO:0043042` | still needs moving — recommend `GO:7770118` |

So the migration work is down to one annotation.

## But a different question now applies to two of them

With `GO:0043041` kept, its name still reads *"for **nonribosomal peptide** biosynthetic process"* — and two of the three experimental annotations are to enzymes that do not make nonribosomal peptides:

- **Aasdh** (PMID:24467666): loads β-alanine onto its own phosphopantetheine site, but *"we hypothesize that it is involved in a rare intracellular reaction, possibly an infrequent post-translational or post-transcriptional modification"*
- **ebony** (PMID:12900414): *"we define Ebony as a beta-alanyl-biogenic amine synthetase"* — β-alanine conjugated to histamine, no peptide formed

**EntF** is the only one that is genuinely nonribosomal peptide biosynthesis (enterobactin).

So rather than a migration question, @LiNiMGI and @hattrill now have a scoping question: is the annotation to an NRP-scoped term correct for an enzyme that does not make an NRP? Three ways out, and it is an editor call rather than yours to resolve alone:

1. keep `GO:0043041` NRP-scoped and move Aasdh and ebony elsewhere
2. broaden `GO:0043041` to amino acid activation onto a carrier protein generally, which would cover all three
3. keep it narrow and mint a broader parent

I have put option 2 forward on #30872.

## Unchanged

All three annotations are well supported for the **molecular function** `GO:7770118 amino acid--[peptidyl-carrier protein] ligase activity` (geneontology/go-ontology#32568, currently open). Adding that MF is worthwhile for all three gene products regardless of how the BP scoping is settled — and `GO:0140414 phosphopantetheine-dependent carrier activity` is also applicable to Aasdh and ebony, which carry their own phosphopantetheine attachment sites.

Still no InterPro2GO, UniRule, HAMAP or MetaCyc mappings to either term.

Apologies for the churn.

author: rozaru
body: I am not sure I got where Claude was going but when I looked at the GO terms, I would propose the following: ``` nonribosomal peptide biosynthetic process |__**amino acid activation for nonribosomal peptide biosynthetic process** (part of) | |__**amino acid adenylylation by nonribosomal peptide synthase** |__tRNA aminoacylation for nonribosomal peptide biosynthetic process (part of) |__glutathione biosynthetic process |__siderophore biosynthetic process |__vancomycin biosynthetic process ``` - [ ] I agree with the original ticket to obsolete GO:0043041 amino acid activation for nonribosomal peptide biosynthetic process GO:0043042 amino acid adenylylation by nonribosomal peptide synthase They both represent an MF (in red in the figure) and it looks like they describe the same reaction. I think that nonribosomal peptide biosynthetic process or the children terms referring to a specific compound are enough. - [ ] Regarding ebony: ebony (e) produces 2 non ribosomal peptides: carcinine (beta-alanine + histamine) and N-β-alanyldopamine (NBAD) (beta-alanine + dopamine). There is no GO term for carcinine biosynthesis which is fine as it is part of the histamine metabolic process. For NBAD, there is a GO term GO:0120576 1,2-dehydro-N-beta-alanyldopamine biosynthetic process recently created which could be added as a child of GO:0019184 nonribosomal peptide biosynthetic process
